<reason>Both sides were sharp, but PRO built the cleaner path. PRO immediately narrowed the motion to harassment/hate/targeted abuse and "refused the bundle" with banter — a framing CON conceded in its first line and never recovered, effectively abandoning the "culture/spontaneity" half of the motion and fighting on efficacy instead. PRO then repeatedly showed that CON's own preferred remedies (human server admins kicking regulars, default-off stranger comms, reputation-weighted matchmaking, new-account gating) are themselves imposed design overriding player preference, which blunts CON's central distinction. CON's best work was real and damaging: the precision-vs-aggression "different dial" attack, the point that every penalty is retrospective too, and the catch that PRO's own verification/match-history gating taxes the same vulnerable players PRO claimed to rescue. CON also answered PRO's pressure questions squarely with the consent distinction and "he loses his audience." But that answer leaves PRO's decisive hole live: under CON's model nothing reaches the proven abuser, and CON's closing concession that "the newcomer never enters that room" reads as institutionalizing exactly the selection mechanism PRO identified in its opening — PRO's "it automates it" line lands. PRO also handled CON's Q1/Q2 honestly (yes with appeals; no identity gate before a strike) rather than dodging. Two clipped CON turns cost the end of its opening and second rebuttal, an execution cost. Close but a clear edge to PRO.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's pressure question demanding a named consequence for the proven slur-spammer, and CON's answer that he merely "loses his audience," which PRO converted in closing into "one system occasionally punishes the wrong player and fixes it; the other never punishes the right one." CON's strongest counterpunch — that PRO's case is really about *better*, not *more aggressive*, enforcement, and that PRO's verification gating hits the vulnerable first — damaged PRO but did not close the no-consequence hole.</best_rebuttal>
